column2: On the authority of Abū Burdah, from his father, Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, “that the Prophet sent him to Yemen, and he asked him about drinks that were made there.
He said: And what are they?
Abū Burdah was asked: What is al-bitʿ?
He said: Honey wine, and al-mizr is barley wine.
He said: Every intoxicant is unlawful.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī.
The printed text reads كل منكر حرام (“every evil is unlawful”), evidently a misprint for كل مسكر حرام (“every intoxicant is unlawful”).

The virtue of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, for the Prophet ﷺ appointed him to a position of authority only because he was capable, perceptive and skilled. That is why ʿUmar, then ʿUthmān, then ʿAlī relied on him—contrary to the Khawārij and the Rāfiḍah, who disparaged him.
The prohibition of consuming any kind of intoxicant, whether made from grape juice or anything else; the hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ on this are mass-transmitted.
A muftī may answer the questioner with more than he asked about, if it is something the questioner needs.
The cause of the prohibition is intoxication, so this requires the prohibition of whatever intoxicates, even if it is not a drink, such as hashish and the like.
